title: Automated 96 Well Plate Protein Quantitation Using Beckman Biomek NxP Workstation
author: ronan o'cualain
materials: Under File, select Open/Method. Select the ProteinQuantitation660nmAssayV01 method.

You will be prompted by the software to enter the location of the first column to be processed. The method is set up to transfer and dilute columns 1 to 10 of the sample plate to the read plate. This is because columns 11 and 12 are used for generating the standard curve. If your first samples are in column A1, enter "1" You will then be prompted to enter the value of the last column to be processed. If you have a full plate of 80 samples, enter "10" . All 80 wells will be processed.

The software will ask you to check that the deck layout matches that of the program. Once you are satisfied that this is the case, click OK. The instrument will now dilute, and add assay reagent to your diluted samples.

You will be prompted by the software to enter the location of the first column to be processed. The method is set up to transfer and dilute columns 1 to 10 of the sample plate to the read plate. This is because columns 11 and 12 are used for generating the standard curve. If your first samples are in column A1, enter "1" You will then be prompted to enter the value of the last column to be processed. If you have a full plate of 80 samples, enter "10" . All 80 wells will be processed.

steps.title: Load sample plate
steps.instruction: Place the sample plate in position P1 of the Biomek deck. Use either a Covaris 96 AFA‑Tube TPX plate (PN 520291) or an 8‑well AFA‑Tube TPX strip (PN 520292) as appropriate.

steps.title: Prepare assay reagent reservoir
steps.instruction: In a Beckman full‑volume reservoir, add 1 g of Ionic Detergent Compatibility Reagent (IDCR) from its packet, then add 50 mL of Pierce 660 nm protein assay reagent. Mix by inverting. Place the reservoir at deck position P4 and label it “AssayReagent”.

steps.title: Prepare diluent reservoir
steps.instruction: Add 50 mL of de‑ionised water to a Beckman full‑volume reservoir, place it at deck position P7 and label it “Diluent”.

steps.title: Load tip boxes onto deck
steps.instruction: Load a box of p250 tips onto position P8, and load two boxes of p20 tips onto positions P2 and P6 of the deck.

steps.title: Place read microplate
steps.instruction: Place a Pierce 96‑well microplate (catalog #15041) onto deck position P3 and label it “Read”.

steps.title: Add BSA calibration standards
steps.instruction: Into columns 11 and 12 of the read plate add the Thermo Scientific Pierce Bovine Serum Albumin Standard Pre‑Diluted Set (catalog 23208). Use the 7 standards ranging from 2 µg/µL to 0.125 µg/µL; reserve the final pair of wells for the diluent blank.

steps.title: Home liquid handler axes
steps.instruction: In the Method tab of the Biomek software, select “Home all axes” to orient and ready the automated liquid handler.

steps.title: Set method volumes and dilution
steps.instruction: Confirm the default sample volume is 120 µL. Set the assay dilution to 1 : 5, meaning 2 µL of sample will be mixed with 8 µL of diluent for each well.

steps.title: Run automated assay
steps.instruction: Start the method by clicking the green Run icon in the Biomek software.

steps.title: Measure absorbance at 660 nm
steps.instruction: After the shaking step completes, measure endpoint absorbance at 660 nm for columns 1‑10 (samples) and columns 11‑12 (calibration curve).

steps.title: Export assay results to CSV
steps.instruction: Export the 660 nm absorbance data to a .csv file for downstream processing.

steps.title: Calculate lysate volumes for 10 µg
steps.instruction: Using the exported data, compute the volume of each lysate needed to obtain 10 µg of protein and add HEPES buffer to bring the final volume to 25 µL (example: lysates measured in wells A1‑H1).

steps.title: Create and upload CSV to transfer file
steps.instruction: Prepare a new .csv file with columns: Source, SourceWell, Dest, DestWell, Volume. Save it, then open the file LysateTransferV01.bmf and upload the .csv in the “File name” tab, ensuring the headers match exactly.
